asked: # Make axHub's Hostinger service load its token from the environment Problem: calls to the `hostinger` service fail with `The credential for "hostinger" is not available` (check with `axhub vault status`). Brett added HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN as a locked runtime env var in Coolify and redeployed, but it still fails. There is no `axhub` CLI inside the axhub-web container. Also check deploy wiring: the Coolify-managed axHub app runs as container `jghxpzuudkahgznvffiwtwmj-*` (redeployed today, built with HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN as a build ARG, which Docker warned about), while a separate `axhub-web` container (axhub-web:latest) has been up for hours. Work out which one actually serves axHub/the MCP connector and say so plainly in the PR. Do this: 1. Find how the vault and service credentials are loaded (code, config, storage location, key naming for `hostinger`). 2. Make the hostinger credential fall back to the `HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN` env var when the vault has no entry (keep vault first). Never log or return the value. 3. Remove HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN from any Dockerfile ARG/ENV so it is runtime-only. 4. If a vault CLI or web page exists, document the exact command/steps to set the credential in the install docs. 5. Add a test for the env fallback. 6. Open a PR with a short, phone-readable description: what was wrong, which container is live, and anything Brett must click in Coolify (exact steps). Do not merge or deploy. Rules: no sub-agents, never print secrets, clean commits. Watch live: Brett can watch the screen you are changing hot-render in the console. Whenever you start work on a screen or element, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "<what you are changing>"` (apps: console-web, axhub-web, amberx-droid, patches-web, walkthrough-studio, demo, framework, console, axhub-android, voicevault). Agent cap: heavy steps (pnpm/npm/vite builds, docker node:22 test runs, Playwright) share a VPS-wide lock. Run each one as `node /opt/axf/deploy/../framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs heavy -- <command>` so only a few run at once.
